admission.justification: Weighed shortening LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS and pooling warm role servers against preserving 60-second serialized cold starts, binding future launch-latency optimizations to measured trace triggers.

alternatives.option: Preserve LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS=60 and per-seat cold-start process isolation for role launches in cli/paseo_role_start.py.
alternatives.reason: 60 seconds accommodates concurrent multi-seat startups under host load without spurious lock-timeout refusals, and per-seat cold starts guarantee isolated agent bindings and clean build-currentness checks (D1008, D1078, 261120-PKG).

alternatives.option: Shorten LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS or share a pre-warmed role-server pool across seat launches (D1008, 261120-PKG).
alternatives.reason: Shortening the wait risks false start-lock refusals under heavy parallel role_start_set bursts, and pooling processes introduces cross-seat binding and stale-build hazards.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Measured multi-seat launch traces show start-lock stalls or cold-start delays exceeding user tolerance under normal load AND a per-seat binding isolation design preserves stale-build and identity guarantees.

consequences: Role starts continue to launch isolated per-seat server processes with launch-time binding confirmation.
context: Each role launch spawns an isolated MCP tool server process and serializes overlapping starts under LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS=60 in cli/paseo_role_start.py. During D1008, 261120-PKG, and Council #6 (D1078), shortening LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS or pooling warm role-server processes was weighed against preserving the 60-second lock budget and per-seat cold-start isolation.
